title: PM vows to boost housing supply
summary: Prime Minister Han Seong-sook on Saturday vowed to increase financial and policy support for development projects to boost housing supply. Han made the remarks as she visited the site of a development project for new homes in Seoul, with the government having pledged to supply more than 230,000 additional homes in the Seoul metropolitan area. During the visit to the development site in Seoul's Seongbuk district, Han emphasized that a speedy supply of new homes is important to stabilize the property market. Han also asked related agencies to use every available means to help construction projects break ground as early as possible.

title: Fires, rescues — and hornet's nests? Korean firefighters face growing burden
summary: A Seoul firefighter surnamed Lee, 33, has good reason to dread hornets. Earlier this month, while removing a hornet's nest in a residential neighborhood, he was stung on the ring finger of his right hand. At first, it felt like a leaf lightly brushing against his skin. But the pain soon became so severe that he could barely tolerate it unless he kept his finger submerged in ice water. "As hornet's nest removal calls increase, the burden on firefighters in the field is also growing," Lee said. "The hornets seem to have become even more aggressive." Removing hornet's nests has long been a routine part of firefighters' work in Korea, but a growing hornet population in urban areas is placing an increasingly heavy burden on emergency crews. title: Less salt, more soul: Korea blends heritage, health at national museum
summary: In a culture where rich, fermented stews and deeply seasoned side dishes define the everyday table, public health officials face a delicate balance: honoring a beloved culinary identity while gently nudging the public toward lighter, lower-sodium eating. The Ministry of Food and Drug Safety offered its latest vision Friday at the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan District, partnering with cultural leaders to frame low-sodium, low-sugar cooking not as a compromise, but as a thoughtful evolution of traditional heritage. At the center of the promotional showcase is "Samsamhan Bapsang" ("The Light & Savory Table"), an annual series of recipe booklets the food safety agency has published since 2012. title: Australian punk rocker Ray Ahn embarks on long, hard journey back to Korea
summary: Australian punk band the Hard-Ons are coming to Korea for the first time in September, but for bassist-vocalist Ray Ahn, it's a return to his birth country. Ahead of the tour, the band released a Korean-language EP, with Ahn singing four of their most memorable songs in Korean, including "Where Did She Come From?" and "Suck and Swallow." Ahn was born in Seoul, and emigrated to Australia at age 9 in 1974 with his family. Now in his early 60s, he still plays for the Hard-Ons, a legendary Sydney punk band known for its multicultural lineup when it was formed in 1982. The band also became notorious because of the name — which shouldn't shock anyone in Korea, where there was once a mainstream band called DickPunks and nobody ever made it weird. title: Why are young Koreans so hooked on Buddhism?
summary: The most striking aspect of the 2026 Busan International Buddhism Expo was its demographic: Hundreds of people in their 20s and 30s packed the booths at BEXCO’s Exhibition Center 1 in Busan on Aug. 9. Young visitors took part in hands-on Buddhist cultural experiences like preparing temple food and performing 108 prostrations. The atmosphere was markedly different from that of other religious events, many attendees said. It was also a far cry from just four or five years ago. The new trend shows young people are experiencing traditional Buddhist culture as something novel and embracing values such as compassion and self-reflection, rather than finding them difficult to understand.
